entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abū l-Ḥajjāj Mujāhid ibn Jabr al-Qāriʾ was a prominent Tabi' and Islamic scholar who played a crucial role in the development of early Islamic thought. Born in Mecca, he studied under the renowned scholar Ibn Ishaq and later became a respected teacher in Medina. His works, including the famous Tafsir al-Qāriʾ, had a profound impact on the interpretation of the Quran and the establishment of the Sunni tradition. He was a close companion of the Third Caliph, Uthman ibn Affan, and was known for his piety, wisdom, and unwavering commitment to the principles of Islam. Despite his significant contributions to Islamic scholarship, Mujāhid's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with few details known about his personal life beyond his academic achievements. His legacy, however, continues to be felt in the world of Islamic studies, with his works remaining a vital source of guidance for scholars and seekers of knowledge alike.
